title: Churned Customers
description: An account is **churned** if it has no login within the 90 days before the **most recent login date in the data** (the system's 'as-of' date). Report every churned account with `account_id` and `last_login` (their most recent login date, or `NULL` if they never logged in). Account ids are unique in `accounts`.
solutionSql:
SELECT a.account_id,
       (SELECT MAX(l.login_date) FROM logins l WHERE l.account_id = a.account_id) AS last_login
FROM accounts a
LEFT JOIN logins l
  ON l.account_id = a.account_id
 AND l.login_date >= date((SELECT MAX(login_date) FROM logins), '-90 days')
WHERE l.account_id IS NULL;
hint: The 90-day window is measured back from the newest login in the table. A LEFT JOIN on 'recent' logins with a NULL check finds accounts that never appear in that window.
outputExplanation: The newest login in the data is today (a fresh login for account 3). Account 1's last login is >90 days before that, so it is churned; account 2 logged in recently and is not.
